headline: Neither AI model reproduced the human framing gap, even with human-like feedback.
verdict: People order about 1.2 units more under own financing (O) than customer financing (C) (three replications pooled; 2.0 in the original study). Claude Haiku 5.5 shows an O − C gap of +0.03 (+0.19 with human-like feedback, not significant) and Llama 3.1 of +0.11. A pooled regression with the human data confirms both gaps are significantly smaller than the human gap. Some alternative wordings give Claude a small gap in the human direction, never close to the human size. In their own words the agents order around average demand and almost never mention the money that moves at order time.
m_agents: 50 agents per model and wording (25 O, 25 C): Claude Haiku 5.5 and Llama 3.1 8B, four wordings each, plus 50 Claude agents with human-like feedback. No personas; instructions word for word from the study.
m_engine: Real dice are rolled by the game engine after each order; payoffs are computed by code and checked (0 rule violations, mean demand 10.5).
m_limits: Agents of one model are not independent; no real stakes; results depend on the model and the wording; the same prompt gave different day-1 orders on different run dates; the profit check is our own addition and few agents pass it.
